title: Shelton stuns Alcaraz in latest-ever US Open finish on September 9
dek: American Ben Shelton defeated defending champion Carlos Alcaraz 6-7 (5), 6-1, 6-3, 1-6, 7-6 (10-7) in a quarterfinal that ended at 3:33 a.m. ET on September 9, the latest finish in US Open history. Shelton advances to face American Frances Tiafoe in the semifinal on September 13, guaranteeing a Black American man will reach the final for the first time since Arthur Ashe in 1972. The U.S. is positioned to win its first men's major title since 2003.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: Shelton beat the No. 1-ranked Alcaraz in a five-set marathon that ended at 3:33 a.m. ET, the latest finish ever at the US Open.
bottom_line: The question for September 13 is whether the 3:33 a.m. finish affects either player's recovery heading into the semifinal; Shelton beat a top-three player for the first time but faces Tiafoe, who is 1-3 against him lifetime but edged him at the 2024 US Open.
body:
Ben Shelton defeated defending champion Carlos Alcaraz 6-7 (5), 6-1, 6-3, 1-6, 7-6 (10-7) in a US Open quarterfinal that finished at 3:33 a.m. ET on September 9, according to ESPN Tennis. The match lasted 4 hours and 28 minutes and started just after 11 p.m., making it the latest finish in US Open history.
Alcaraz's 18-match Grand Slam winning streak ended with the loss, per ESPN Tennis. This was Shelton's first victory over a top-three player, according to ESPN Tennis. Shelton won nine straight games from early in the second set until he had a 3-0 lead in the third. Alcaraz vomited before the final set and held a 5-3 lead in the deciding tiebreaker before Shelton came back, finishing with a 146 mph serve his opponent could not return, per ESPN Tennis.
Shelton is now in his third Grand Slam semifinal, having reached the final four in the 2023 US Open and 2025 Australian Open, per ESPN Tennis. He is the first American to beat the defending US Open champion in five sets since 18-year-old Peter Sampras defeated Mats Wilander in 1989, according to ESPN Tennis. This was Alcaraz's first-ever loss to an American player at a Slam and first defeat at a major to a lefty, per ESPN Tennis.
The Shelton-Tiafoe matchup will be the first major meeting in the semifinals or later between Black American men in the Open era, per ESPN Tennis. One of them will become the first Black American man to reach a US Open final since Arthur Ashe in 1972, per ESPN Tennis.
Alcaraz's run back from a five-month absence due to a right wrist injury shaped the match. He said he felt "really tired" in the third set and was "physically really tired" overall, per ESPN Tennis. Alcaraz noted his goal was "to leave the tournament having played matches and staying healthy", suggesting the injury comeback was the priority.
The late finish highlighted scheduling concerns across the tournament. All four quarterfinal matches on September 9 extended to the deciding set, per Front Office Sports. Venus Williams was upset about the 12:13 a.m. start time of her first round match against Sofia Kenin, saying "I just don't know any other sport where you have to start that late... I definitely think there's room for improvement there," according to Front Office Sports. Jessica Pegula questioned whether there was "just a better way or just starting an hour earlier or just something different," per Front Office Sports. Tennis Channel CEO Jeff Blackburn called late-night finishes "a defect that needs to get addressed," according to Front Office Sports.
The U.S. is guaranteed to have a representative in Sunday's final and is seeking its first men's major title since Andy Roddick won the 2003 US Open, per ESPN Tennis. Shelton owns a career 3-1 record over Tiafoe, including their most recent meeting in Washington D.C. last summer, per ESPN Tennis. They have split their two previous US Open clashes, with Shelton defeating Tiafoe in 2023 to reach his first major semifinal and Tiafoe returning the favor in the 2024 round of 32, per ESPN Tennis. Shelton is a former national champion and player of the year at Florida, per ESPN Tennis.
